steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: Import the fs/promises module for file operations and node-cron for scheduling tasks. Use the 'import' statement to import these modules.
steps.hint: You'll need to import fs/promises for file system operations and node-cron for scheduling. Use the ES module syntax: import moduleName from 'module-name'.

steps.title: Define the data retention period constant
steps.instruction: Below the imports, create a constant named RETENTION_DAYS to define how many days old files should be kept before cleanup. Set its value to 30.
steps.hint: Use the const keyword to declare a constant variable. Assign it a numeric value representing days.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: defining a configuration constant
const MAX_FILE_SIZE = 1024;
steps.seedCode:
// Import fs/promises and node-cron modules here

// Define RETENTION_DAYS constant here
steps.expectedOutcome: A constant RETENTION_DAYS with value 30 is defined for the cleanup task configuration.
successCriteria: The constant RETENTION_DAYS is declared with const and set to 30.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the data retention period constant. This configuration value will control how old files need to be before they're cleaned up.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the constant is named exactly RETENTION_DAYS and has the value 30.
steps.feedbackWrong: The constant definition is missing or incorrect. Create a constant named RETENTION_DAYS with the value 30.

steps.title: Create the directory path constant
steps.instruction: Define a constant named DATA_DIR_PATH that contains the path to the directory where your data files are stored. Use a string with the path './data'.
steps.hint: You can create a constant using the 'const' keyword followed by the name and assignment.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: defining a directory path constant
const UPLOADS_DIR = './uploads';
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a constant DATA_DIR_PATH set to './data' that will be used later to locate files for cleanup.
successCriteria: DATA_DIR_PATH constant is defined with the value './data'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the directory path constant. This will be used to locate the files that need cleanup.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a constant, but make sure it's named exactly DATA_DIR_PATH and has the value './data'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The constant is not defined correctly. Please define a constant named DATA_DIR_PATH with the value './data'.

steps.title: Define the calculateCutoffDate function
steps.instruction: Create a function named calculateCutoffDate that calculates the cutoff date by subtracting RETENTION_DAYS from the current date and returns that date.
steps.hint: You can create a new Date object for the current date, then use setDate() to subtract the retention days. Return the resulting Date object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The calculateCutoffDate function should be defined and return a Date object representing the cutoff date.
successCriteria: A function named calculateCutoffDate is created that uses RETENTION_DAYS and returns a Date object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the calculateCutoffDate function that calculates the retention cutoff date.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function subtracts RETENTION_DAYS from the current date and returns the resulting Date object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The calculateCutoffDate function is missing or doesn't correctly calculate the cutoff date. Review how to subtract days from a Date object.

steps.title: Create the cleanupOldFiles function
steps.instruction: Define an async function named cleanupOldFiles that will handle the core file cleanup logic. This function should be empty for now - we'll implement the logic in later steps.
steps.hint: Use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Remember to mark it as async since it will eventually work with file operations.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an empty async function named cleanupOldFiles defined in your code.
successCriteria: An async function named cleanupOldFiles is defined in the code.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the cleanupOldFiles function. This will be the core function that handles identifying and removing old files.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've defined an async function named cleanupOldFiles.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cleanupOldFiles function isn't defined yet. Create an async function with that name.

steps.title: Add file age checking logic
steps.instruction: Inside the cleanupOldFiles function, add logic to check if each file's last modified date is older than the cutoff date.
steps.hint: You'll need to compare the file's mtime (modification time) with the cutoff date. Use the Date object for comparison.
steps.expectedOutcome: The cleanupOldFiles function will have logic to compare each file's modification time with the cutoff date.
successCriteria: The function contains code that checks if a file's last modified date is older than the cutoff date.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the file age checking logic. This is essential for identifying which files need to be cleaned up.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're comparing the file's modification time with the cutoff date.
steps.feedbackWrong: The file age checking logic is missing or incorrect. You need to compare each file's mtime with the cutoff date.

steps.title: Add file deletion logic
steps.instruction: Inside the cleanupOldFiles function, after the file age checking logic comment, add code to delete files that are older than the retention period.
steps.hint: You'll need to iterate through the files array, check each file's stats to get its modification time, compare it with the cutoffDate, and use fs.unlink to delete old files.
steps.expectedOutcome: The cleanupOldFiles function will now include logic to identify and delete files older than the retention period.
successCriteria: The function contains a loop that checks file modification times and deletes files older than cutoffDate using fs.unlink.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the file deletion logic. The function now identifies old files and removes them from the filesystem.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the deletion logic needs more work. Make sure you're comparing file modification times with cutoffDate and using fs.unlink to delete old files.
steps.feedbackWrong: The file deletion logic is missing or incorrect. Review the example and try again - you need to check file ages and delete those older than the retention period.

steps.title: Add error handling to cleanup function
steps.instruction: Inside the cleanupOldFiles function, add a try-catch block around the file reading operation to handle potential errors when accessing the data directory.
steps.hint: Wrap the existing 'const files = await fs.readdir(DATA_DIR_PATH);' line with try-catch. The catch block should log the error with console.error.
steps.expectedOutcome: The cleanupOldFiles function will have proper error handling for the directory reading operation, making it more robust.
successCriteria: The try-catch block wraps the fs.readdir call and logs errors appropriately.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added error handling to make the file reading operation more robust.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the try-catch block properly wraps the file reading operation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error handling isn't quite right. Remember to wrap the fs.readdir call in a try-catch block.

steps.title: Set up the scheduled task
steps.instruction: Use node-cron's schedule method to run the cleanupOldFiles function daily at midnight (cron pattern '0 0 * * *').
steps.hint: Call cron.schedule() with the cron pattern as the first argument and your cleanup function as the second argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: The cleanup function will be scheduled to run automatically every day at midnight.
successCriteria: cron.schedule is called with pattern '0 0 * * *' and cleanupOldFiles as the callback.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully scheduled the cleanup task to run daily at midnight.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling cron.schedule with the correct cron pattern and passing cleanupOldFiles as the callback.
steps.feedbackWrong: The scheduled task isn't set up correctly. Use cron.schedule() to run cleanupOldFiles daily at midnight.

steps.title: Add startup logging
steps.instruction: Add a console.log statement right after the cron.schedule call to indicate the cleanup task has started successfully.
steps.hint: Use console.log with a descriptive message like 'Cleanup task scheduled to run daily at midnight'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The console will display a startup message confirming the cleanup task is scheduled when the script runs.
successCriteria: A console.log statement is added after the cron.schedule call with a message about the cleanup task starting.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The startup logging provides clear feedback that the cleanup task is active.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added logging, but make sure it's placed right after the cron.schedule call and has a descriptive message about the task starting.
steps.feedbackWrong: The startup logging is missing. Add a console.log statement after the cron.schedule call to indicate the task has started.
